## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: waiting periods, test sets by applicant type, late-arrival wording, and the remaining test-vehicle and road test observation items
Confusable pairs among the waiting periods and the test sets that different applicants take, followed by continuation facts on documents, equipment checks and what the examiner watches; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
Waiting periods differ by cause: a failed knowledge test means a one-day wait, while being caught cheating means a 30-day wait before another attempt. [A01]
Why it matters: group retakes; confusable failure wait versus cheating wait.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
Exchanging a Class PD permit for a Class D license needs only the vision screening and road skills test, while a duplicate or renewal needs no test at all. [A01]
Why it matters: group test sets; confusable exchange versus renewal.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A01
Adding a For-Hire endorsement requires the vision screening and a knowledge test. [A01]
Why it matters: group test sets; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A01
Anyone returning to retake a test must bring all the required original documents again. [A01]
Why it matters: group retakes; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A01
When a deaf applicant asks for an oral knowledge test, the Department of Safety supplies a certified sign language interpreter to help administer it. [A01]
Why it matters: group accommodations; confusable interpreter ban versus sign language exception.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A01
Forms of cheating include written notes on paper, clothing, the body or devices, talking during the test including phone use, and trying to have someone else take the exam. [A01]
Why it matters: group conduct; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A01
All cell phones, pagers and text messaging devices must be switched off during both the written test and the road test. [A01]
Why it matters: group conduct; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A02
An applicant without a valid Tennessee learner permit must bring proof of US citizenship or lawful permanent residency to the road test appointment, or current proof of temporary legal presence when getting a TDL. [A02]
Why it matters: group road test documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A02
Before the road test the applicant must show how to use eight equipment items, including the windshield defroster and fan to defog the glass. [A02]
Why it matters: group vehicle check; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle used for the road test must have a working horn and valid registration tags. [A02]
Why it matters: group vehicle check; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A02
The Department may cancel road test appointments during emergencies or dangerous weather. [A02]
Why it matters: group road test logistics; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A03
On a multi-purpose vehicle, windows behind the front seat are exempt from tint limits, but the windows to the driver's left and right follow the passenger car rule. [A03]
Why it matters: group vehicle check; confusable passenger car versus multi-purpose tint.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A03
The test vehicle needs a muffler to prevent excessive noise and smoke, a working speedometer, and driver and passenger doors that open from both inside and outside. [A03]
Why it matters: group vehicle check; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A03
The examiner watches how you prepare and start, control the car, handle intersections and turns, obey signals and signs, drive in traffic, stop, back up, judge distance, signal to others, share the road and adjust speed. [A03]
Why it matters: group road test scoring; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A03
After a failed road test the examiner explains the errors, how to correct them and which maneuvers to practice before returning. [A03]
Why it matters: group road test scoring; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A04
Bring a familiar vehicle whose horn, lights, belts, brakes, signals and wipers all work and whose registration is current. [A04]
Why it matters: group road test logistics; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A04
The Tennessee PID App lets an eligible proctor obtain a secure personal identification verified against the proctor's own Department of Safety record before supervising an online knowledge test. [A04]
Why it matters: group online testing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0038]
